findings.summary: Lag and rolling features (shift(1), shift(7), rolling mean) are computed over the whole frame rather than per store_id, leaking data across stores, and dropna only removes the first 7 rows overall so contaminated rows remain.
Code assumes rows are sorted by date with no missing days; without sorting by store_id and date, lag7 is not the same weekday last week when days are missing.
build_features requires a sales column, so a future-dated prediction frame without sales raises KeyError, and if sales are NaN the dropna removes exactly the rows to be predicted.
Multi-step forecasts need recursive or other handling for lag1 and mean7 beyond day +1, and none of this is covered by tests.
test_calendar_features passes only by coincidence: with n=10, 7 rows are dropped so loc[0] is 2026-01-08, also a Thursday; it no longer tests the first date and will break if the lag window changes.
test_lag_features uses a single store so it cannot catch the cross-store leakage bug; a two-store test is needed.
